about.p.1: The Korean Medical Tourism Promotion Association is a platform leading the globalization of K-Medi, working alongside member organizations, professionals and government to establish Korea as a global medical tourism hub.
about.p.2: Korea has moved beyond an era defined solely by advanced medical technology. Today it is drawing global attention for creating an entirely new kind of value — 'K-Medi' — where Korean culture, tourism and wellness come together as one.
about.div.1: New vision is the art of seeing the unseen.
about.p.3: True innovation begins with discovering the possibilities hidden beneath what is visible. As a public-interest corporation under the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and an international non-governmental organization built around Korea's advanced medical expertise and the people behind it, our association combines physician-led professionalism with a strong member network to practise the 'Art of Vision' — designing the future of Korean medical tourism.
about.p.4: First, creating distinctive value through convergence. Beyond treatment alone, we will build a medical tourism model unlike any other, where patients experience Korea's high-quality healthcare and compelling culture together, and find new energy for their lives.
about.p.5: Second, building a sustainable ecosystem through shared growth. Grounded in transparent governance and credible accountability, we will form a network in which some 200 member organizations grow together — an industry ecosystem resilient enough to withstand changes in the external environment.
about.p.6: Our association will devote every capability to becoming the platform that leads the globalization of K-Medi and firmly establishes Korea as a global medical tourism hub. We look forward to your interest and active participation on this journey to uncover unseen value and draw a larger future for Korean medical tourism.
about.div.2: Chairman, Korean Medical Tourism Promotion Association
about.p.7: As the No.1 global partner for K-medical tourism trusted beyond Korea, we work to make Korean healthcare the first name international patients think of when they think of trust.
about.h3.1:
Transparency and public interest
as the industry standard.
about.p.8: To contribute to better health for people and to national economic development by advancing transparency in medical tourism and spreading its public value.
about.p.9: Trust · Coexistence · Innovation · Public Interest — the promises that guide everything we do.
about.p.10: "Unshakeable confidence, built on transparent operations and professionalism"
about.p.11: We treat advancing transparency in the medical tourism industry and earning international trust as our highest priority. Grounded in professional medical knowledge and rigorous ethics, we are establishing a standard for Korean medical tourism that every stakeholder, at home and abroad, can choose with confidence.
about.p.12: "A partnership that connects healthcare and culture, and grows together with partners"
about.p.13: As a powerful network hub connecting medical institutions, beauty and tourism businesses, and government ministries, we create complementary synergies. By fostering a healthy business ecosystem in which every member and partner grows and shares in the benefits, we drive the shared growth of medical tourism.
about.p.14: "Designing a new future for medical tourism by discovering unseen possibilities"
about.p.15: Guided by the philosophy that 'new vision is the art of seeing the unseen', we present a new vision for K-Medical through creative approaches that break existing moulds. By organically combining advanced medical technology with Korean cultural content, we lead an innovative medical tourism model that draws global attention.
about.p.16: "Advancing global health and spreading sustainable value"
about.p.17: Beyond promoting an industry, we act as an international NGO and public-interest corporation that fulfils its social responsibilities, including medical welfare support for vulnerable populations at home and abroad. By contributing to national economic development and to better health and welfare for people everywhere, we realise sustainable public value.
about.p.18: Under the general assembly and the board of directors, the chairman represents the association and the secretary-general oversees day-to-day operations. Three divisions — medical, tourism and beauty — together with the secretariat, are responsible for programmes in their respective fields.

transparency.p.1: KMTPA delivers the goodwill of our supporters transparently and fairly.
transparency.p.2: The Korean Medical Tourism Promotion Association practises sustainable management grounded in public value and industry development. Through transparent governance, credible accountability and the participation of diverse stakeholders, we contribute to a resilient and sustainable medical tourism ecosystem in Korea.
transparency.p.3: KMTPA operates on the conviction that medical tourism must go beyond economic activity to create social value grounded in public benefit and trust. By fostering a transparent industry environment and operating responsibly, we aim to build a world-class medical tourism ecosystem and contribute to public health and national competitiveness.
transparency.div.1: Explore KMTPA's vision and mission Meet KMTPA's leadership
transparency.p.4: KMTPA pursues fair and trusted operations through a governance system built on responsibility and transparency. As an incorporated association, we establish and pursue key policies and business directions through a decision-making structure centred on the general assembly and the board of directors in accordance with relevant legislation. Through our management systems we also implement strategies for the sound development and global competitiveness of Korean medical tourism and related industries, expanding domestic and international cooperation networks on the basis of trust in the K-medical tourism sector — sustainable operations in which public benefit and industry development are held in balance.
transparency.div.2: Explore the KMTPA organization
transparency.p.5: KMTPA reflects on-the-ground views in its policies and programmes through dialogue and cooperation with a wide range of stakeholders, including medical institutions, medical tourists, government and local communities. In doing so we promote qualitative growth in the industry while fulfilling public-interest roles such as creating patient-centred service environments and supporting vulnerable groups. We realise both the economic impact of a thriving industry and the creation of social value, contributing to a sustainable medical tourism ecosystem.
transparency.div.3: What KMTPA does KMTPA's key activities
transparency.p.6: As a non-profit corporation serving the public interest, the Korean Medical Tourism Promotion Association places transparency and accountability at the heart of its financial management. All funds are managed systematically in accordance with relevant legislation and internal regulations, and the entire process — from budgeting through execution to settlement — is disclosed. This strengthens stakeholder trust and supports sustainable operations grounded in public benefit and financial soundness.
transparency.p.7: We disclose the results of our annual financial operations. Income, expenditure and programme-level spending show how funds have been used.
transparency.div.4: Request KMTPA financial statements Request the KMTPA audit report
transparency.p.8: We set out our annual budget and how funds are allocated across major programmes, so you can see our planned financial direction and priorities.
transparency.div.5: Request the KMTPA budget plan Explore KMTPA's programmes and activities
transparency.p.9: KMTPA discloses how donations and sponsorship are raised and spent, so you can see transparent management and public-interest use of funds.
transparency.div.6: Request fundraising and utilisation records KMTPA public-interest corporation disclosures (National Tax Service)
transparency.p.10: As a non-profit corporation serving the public interest, the Korean Medical Tourism Promotion Association holds transparency and accountability as core principles across its operations. We disclose information on finances, programmes and decision-making in good faith, and take responsibility for the outcomes. On this basis of stakeholder trust, we aim to contribute to a sustainable environment for the medical tourism industry.
transparency.p.11: As the role and influence of non-profit organizations grows internationally, expectations around transparency and accountability continue to rise. International standards such as the United Nations Global Compact and the Global Reporting Initiative serve as important guidance for disclosing operations and performance and for building stakeholder trust. The INGO Accountability Charter, jointly adopted by international NGOs in 2006, is regarded as an early global common standard for strengthening accountability and transparency in the non-profit sector, and has since spread into a range of international frameworks.
transparency.div.7: Request INGO Accountability Charter materials
transparency.p.12: In Korea too, as public expectations of non-profit accountability rise, financial disclosure and transparent management of programme outcomes have become important benchmarks. In international development and in the medical and health fields in particular, more organizations are adopting operating and reporting systems aligned with global standards, with growing emphasis on stakeholder participation and management of social impact. Amid these changes, the association practises transparent management in line with international trends and works to strengthen the credibility and sustainability of Korea's medical tourism industry.
transparency.div.8: Request the KCOC NGO accountability self-assessment
transparency.p.13: KMTPA operates channels for feedback and reports in support of transparent and responsible operations. If you have suggestions for improvement or become aware of anything inappropriate, please let us know and we will review the matter and act in good faith in line with our procedures.
transparency.div.9: Report tax evasion (National Tax Service) Report corruption or public-interest violations (ACRC)

home.p.1: Eight areas of work that protect both our members' professionalism and our patients' trust.
home.p.2: We review and accredit member medical institutions that meet international healthcare service standards, giving patients a benchmark they can choose with confidence.
home.p.3: We run certification programmes for medical tourism coordinators and interpreters, ensuring consistency and professionalism in patient care.
home.p.4: We publish research on the industry's core issues, including the international patient system, medical visas and price transparency for non-covered treatments.
home.p.5: Through partnerships with overseas governments, medical institutions and insurers, we support Korean healthcare abroad and the attraction of international patients.
home.p.6: We continuously gather medical tourism news from Korea and abroad, summarise each week's developments and implications, and deliver them to members by newsletter.
home.p.7: We respond in multiple languages from the earliest stage of care decisions, connecting patients with the right member institution and a certified coordinator.
home.p.8: We collect members' international patient figures, organise them by specialty and country, and provide them as an evidence base for business planning.
home.p.9: Through regular forums and practitioner seminars, we create spaces where institutions, coordinators and agencies meet to share cases and know-how.
home.p.10: Each month we bring you industry trends, member news and policy insight.

patient-journey.h1.1:
Treatment in Korea,
how does it work?
patient-journey.p.1: From preparation to care after you return home — the association and its member institutions guide you at every stage. Every step is supported by accredited institutions and association-certified coordinators.
patient-journey.p.2: Before you decide on treatment, your medical records are shared with Korean clinicians in advance and you receive an initial opinion on diagnosis and treatment direction. At this stage your appointment schedule, expected costs, companion details and medical visa procedures are all set out.
patient-journey.div.1: Association support We find and connect you with the member institution that fits your needs, and guide you through advance translation of your home-country medical records and the medical visa process (C-3-3 short stay / G-1-10 long-term treatment).
patient-journey.p.3: An association-certified coordinator accompanies you from arrival at Incheon or Gimpo Airport through to the medical institution. Immigration, your welcome meeting and hotel check-in all proceed safely and without confusion.
patient-journey.div.2: Association support A certified member coordinator meets you on arrival and guides you to accommodation partnered with your member institution. A 24-hour emergency hotline is operated jointly by the association and member institutions.
patient-journey.p.4: Your treatment plan is confirmed through an in-person assessment with clinicians. Every stage of care is translated into a language you understand, and treatment options, duration, costs and risks are provided in writing.
patient-journey.div.3: Association support Interpretation in English, Chinese, Russian, Arabic and other languages is provided jointly by member institutions and association-certified coordinators. Our standard consent form makes treatment options, costs and risks explicit, and where needed the association can arrange a second opinion from another member institution.
patient-journey.p.5: Care begins according to the agreed plan. Member institutions follow association accreditation standards for patient safety, infection control and record-keeping, and progress is shared with both your companion and the association.
patient-journey.div.4: Association support Accredited member institutions deliver care under the association's standard protocols. The association separately monitors that patients' rights are being upheld and, should a dispute arise, helps resolve it through a formal mediation process.
patient-journey.p.6: Clinical monitoring continues throughout inpatient or outpatient recovery. Your recovery environment — accommodation, diet and transport — and your follow-up schedule are adjusted to your condition.
patient-journey.div.5: Association support Member institutions advise on accommodation and diet suited to your recovery period and arrange follow-up appointments in advance. Support for companions staying with you continues without interruption.
patient-journey.p.7: Before you fly home, your final clinical summary, medication guidance and follow-up schedule are prepared in your language. The association also helps arrange remote consultation with your clinicians at home after you return.
patient-journey.div.6: Association support Member institutions issue an English-language clinical summary, and the association provides standard guidance on taking prescribed medicines out of the country. After you return home, the association connects your local clinicians with the member institution for remote consultation.
patient-journey.h2.7: What should you prepare for your visit?
patient-journey.p.8: Everything other than treatment — entry, transport, accommodation, language. The association and its members keep what you have to worry about to a minimum.
patient-journey.li.1: International airportsDirect flights to Incheon (ICN), Gimpo (GMP), Gimhae (PUS) and Jeju (CJU)
patient-journey.li.2: Airport pickupAccompanied by member institutions and certified coordinators
patient-journey.li.3: Getting aroundKTX high-speed rail, subway, taxi and private shuttle
patient-journey.li.4: Wheelchair supportStep-free routes at airports, stations and medical institutions
patient-journey.li.5: Hotels near the hospitalRecovery-friendly rooms and dietary options
patient-journey.li.6: Serviced apartmentsSuited to longer stays and accompanying family
patient-journey.li.7: Korean medicine wellness resortsRecovery programmes in Jeju, Gangwon and other natural settings
patient-journey.li.8: Partner ratesPreferential rates for member institution patients
patient-journey.li.9: InterpretationEnglish, Chinese, Russian, Arabic, Japanese, Mongolian and more
patient-journey.li.11: Multilingual consent formsTreatment options, costs and risks in writing
patient-journey.p.9: The association's role does not end when treatment does. Together with member institutions, we take responsibility for your recovery and follow-up care at home.
patient-journey.div.7: Remote consultation with your local clinicians The association arranges telemedicine consultation between the Korean clinicians who treated you and your doctor at home.
patient-journey.div.8: Taking prescribed medicines home We advise on which medicines may be taken out of the country, customs documentation, and English-language prescriptions where required.
patient-journey.div.9: Follow-up scheduling Regular follow-ups, return visits and video consultations are coordinated jointly by member institutions and certified coordinators.
patient-journey.div.10: Mediation if a dispute arises For care-related issues arising after you return home, the association provides a formal mediation process between the member institution and the patient.
patient-journey.button.1: What documents should I prepare before departure?
patient-journey.div.11: At minimum: your passport, a medical visa (if applicable), medical records from home (in English or translated into Korean), a copy of your insurance certificate, and companion details. Exact requirements vary slightly by member institution, and your coordinator will provide a checklist in advance.
patient-journey.div.12: Member institutions provide interpretation in major languages including English, Chinese, Russian and Arabic. For less common languages, the association matches you with an interpreter from its pool of certified coordinators.
patient-journey.button.3: Can a companion stay with me?
patient-journey.div.13: Yes. Most member institutions allow a companion to stay during inpatient care, and for outpatient treatment you can stay together at partner accommodation. Your coordinator will also advise on your companion's visa and stay procedures.
patient-journey.button.4: How long do I need to stay in Korea?
patient-journey.div.14: It depends on the type of treatment. Short screenings and procedures typically take 3–7 days, while surgery requiring recovery usually takes 2–6 weeks or more. Your member institution will confirm the exact schedule at the consultation stage.
patient-journey.button.5: Can I receive care after returning home?
patient-journey.div.15: Yes. An English clinical summary and prescription details are provided to your clinicians at home, and follow-up consultations can continue by telemedicine where needed. The association also helps connect your local clinicians.
patient-journey.h2.10: Ready to take the next step?
patient-journey.p.10: Find a member institution or contact the association to begin your preparations.

together.h1.1: The association is made by its members
together.p.1: Korean medical tourism does not run on the strength of one hospital or one company. Patients feel safe only when those who treat, those who guide and those who host all stand on the same standard. The association is where that standard is built together.
together.h2.1:
We don't broker deals.
We set standards.
together.p.2: Handing patients to hospitals for a commission is not the association's business. As a public-interest corporation under the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, we build the standards and channels through which members can prove their own trustworthiness.
together.p.3: We do not steer patients toward any particular institution. The association's name is not a sales tool for one organization — it is a shared asset of the whole industry.
together.p.4: Membership does not end with an application. We review business registration and other documents before granting approval. Being a member should mean having been checked.
together.p.5: We publish our finances and activities through National Tax Service public-interest corporation disclosures. Members should be able to see where their fees have gone.
together.p.6: Neither treatment alone nor guidance alone completes medical tourism. The association brings together the organizations responsible for each stage of the journey.
together.p.7: Hospitals and clinics treating international patients, presenting their clinical capability against international standards.
together.p.8: Registered agencies that meet patients, advise them and design their itineraries.
together.p.9: Hotel, travel and transport operators responsible for stays and journeys before and after treatment.
together.p.10: Public agencies and associations that build the industry's foundations through policy, research and education.
together.p.11: Added to these are individual professionals — medical coordinators, medical interpreters, medical tourism and international healthcare practitioners, and research and education specialists. The people who actually meet patients on the ground are the basis for the association's judgement.
together.p.12: Required documents and benefits differ by membership type.

programs.p.1: Connecting data and practice to set the next standard for K-medical tourism. Korea has already entered the era of one million international patients a year. The association designs what comes after quantitative growth — trust, quality, regional reach, skilled professionals and public responsibility.

programs.h3.9: Trust matters more than the pace of growth
programs.p.11: According to figures from the Ministry of Health and Welfare and the Korea Health Industry Development Institute, 1.17 million international patients visited Korea in 2024 — a 93.2% increase on 2023. Since the international patient programme began in 2009, cumulative patients have reached 5.05 million, from 202 countries. The industry's task is now shifting beyond simply attracting more patients toward patient safety, accurate information, care before and after treatment, and balanced growth across regions and specialties.
programs.div.2: Cumulative patients 5.05 million Since the programme began in 2009
programs.div.3: Countries of origin 202 Japan, China, USA, Taiwan, Thailand lead
programs.div.4: Key challenge Qualitative growth Trust, regional spread, structured aftercare
programs.p.12: Sources: Ministry of Health and Welfare, "1.17 million international patients in 2024: Korea emerges as Asia's medical tourism hub"; Korea Health Industry Development Institute, "2024 International Patient Statistics Report".
programs.h3.10: Turning country-level demand into trusted consultations and visits
programs.p.13: The 2024 figures show demand recovering rapidly across East Asia, the Americas and Southeast Asia. Japan and China together accounted for 60.0% of all international patients, while Taiwan rose 550.6% year on year. At the same time, patients from the United States used a broader range of specialties — not only dermatology but also integrated internal medicine and screening centres. The association analyses these differing patterns of demand and decision-making so that our members' strengths reach each market through the right language and channels.
programs.div.5: Our approach Rather than untargeted exposure, what matters is information designed around each market's patient journey, matching with trustworthy institutions, and quality control in pre-treatment consultation.
programs.div.6: Market strategy by country We differentiate priority specialties and messaging by market — dermatology, aesthetics and wellness demand in Japan, Taiwan and China; screening, internal medicine and complex care in the United States; screening and treatment in Russia and Central Asia.
programs.div.7: Trust-based content We produce multilingual content covering what patients actually want to know: clinicians' expertise, the care process, expected length of stay, interpretation support and aftercare.
programs.div.8: Overseas roadshows and B2B matching We run business meetings with overseas medical institutions, insurers, travel agencies, patient-attraction operators and public agencies, helping members meet suitable partners.
programs.div.9: Stronger enquiry and consultation channels We refine initial guidance and handover criteria so that enquiries arriving via the website, social media, trade fairs and local partners lead through to specialist consultation, appointments and travel preparation.
programs.div.10: Linking healthcare, wellness and tourism Considering recovery before and after treatment, companions' stays and regional tourism assets together, we develop models that improve the whole experience for patients and their families.
programs.h3.11: Managing a fast-growing market into a sustainable industry
programs.p.14: In its 2023 strategy for international patient attraction, the government identified improved immigration procedures, reduced concentration by region and specialty, stronger industry competitiveness and greater global recognition of Korean healthcare as key tasks. In 2024, the 700,000-patient target set for 2027 was exceeded well ahead of schedule — but structural features also became clear: 85.4% concentration in Seoul, 56.6% in dermatology, and 82.0% treated at clinic-level institutions. Working from this data, the association translates on-the-ground challenges into policy language and helps members respond to change ahead of time.
programs.div.11: Our approach Industry growth must be balanced with public access to healthcare, patient safety, regional spread, and sound legal and regulatory frameworks.
programs.div.12: Regular market reports We analyse patient flows by country, changes by specialty, regional patterns and institution types, providing material that members and policymakers can use together.
programs.div.13: Regulatory monitoring We track changes that affect day-to-day practice, including the Act on Overseas Expansion of Healthcare, the Medical Service Act, personal data protection, advertising rules, medical tourism visas, and registration and reporting duties for attraction agencies.
programs.div.14: Patient safety and service quality research We research the standards that build trust in services for international patients: pre-treatment explanation, cost estimates, interpretation quality, consent, dispute prevention and aftercare.
programs.div.15: Diversifying regions and specialties We propose models that connect demand concentrated in Seoul and particular specialties with regional healthcare, screening, Korean medicine, dentistry, rehabilitation and wellness.
programs.div.16: Policy roundtables and field recommendations We gather views from member institutions, attraction agencies, local governments and experts, and bring practice-based recommendations to government and public agencies.
programs.h3.12: The quality patients feel is decided by readiness on the ground
programs.p.15: In 2024, clinic-level institutions accounted for 82.0% of international patients — the largest share. This reflects rapid growth in short outpatient visits and aesthetic and wellness demand, and it also means that standards for treating international patients are needed at many more sites. The association runs training and assessment systems so that clinicians, international healthcare centres, coordinators, interpreters and consultation staff all work to the same standard.
programs.div.17: Our approach Good clinical outcomes alone are not enough. Trust must be managed across the whole process — explanation, interpretation, scheduling, costs, consent and recovery guidance.
programs.div.18: Medical tourism coordinator programme Covers the whole patient journey: initial consultation, appointments, pre-arrival guidance, navigating the hospital, explaining costs, supporting companions, and follow-up after the patient returns home.
programs.div.19: Medical interpretation and cultural communication Beyond conveying words, we strengthen professional interpretation so that explanations of illness, procedural risks, consent and recovery precautions are understood without misunderstanding.
programs.div.20: Readiness assessment for member institutions We review multilingual guidance, standard consent forms, consultation records, emergency contact systems, aftercare protocols and complaint procedures.
programs.div.21: Practical training on registration and reporting We help members understand statutory duties and operational practice, including registration requirements for international patient attraction agencies, annual performance reporting and personal data management.
programs.div.22: Sharing best practice and standard manuals We build up cases from member institutions and develop them into response manuals by specialty, language group and patient type, shared as training material.
programs.h3.13: Extending growth into the right to health and public value
programs.p.16: Medical tourism is a high-value industry combining healthcare and travel — but it also deals with people's health and lives. The government has identified charitable care and training for overseas clinicians as ways to raise global recognition of Korean healthcare. The association brings together members' expertise to reach those with limited access to treatment, and runs public-interest programmes so that Korean healthcare builds social trust alongside commercial success.
programs.div.23: Our approach Public-interest work should not be one-off sponsorship, but a system that continuously connects access to care, education, prevention and recovery support.
programs.div.24: Charitable care at home and abroad We identify patients with limited access to treatment for economic or geographic reasons and work with member institutions to connect them with consultations and care.
programs.div.25: Training and knowledge exchange for overseas clinicians We run training, seminars and clinical exchange for clinicians from partner countries, contributing to local healthcare capacity.
programs.div.26: Prevention, screening and recovery campaigns We jointly plan campaigns that draw on members' expertise in health screening, chronic disease prevention, rehabilitation, mental health and wellness.
programs.div.27: Support for vulnerable groups in Korea We provide consultation, interpretation and care referral information to multicultural families, migrants, foreign workers and others who find health information hard to access.
programs.div.28: Social impact reporting We record and publish who our social contribution work reaches, how it is delivered and what it achieves, building a public-interest system that supporters and members can trust.
programs.p.17: The path the association has taken.
